note: Operator-depth ratchet baseline. `current` is the measured state at plan time, re-derived
from source by scripts/check-depth.mjs. Floors may only rise, ceilings may only fall.
`phases` declares every phase's numeric exit target UP FRONT, before implementation. That
ordering is the point: a target invented after the work cannot fail. Run
`node scripts/check-depth.mjs --phase P3` to certify a phase. A phase with no declared
target cannot be certified at all - the gate exits 2 rather than passing.
Targets were derived from the per-module gap in RICHNESS-JOIN.json, not chosen for comfort.
Desktop operator surface is 5107 fields; the web starts at 1731; the 3376-field difference is
distributed across the phases below and must sum to parity by P11.

descriptorSurface.basis: Additive static descriptor candidates reached from returned JSX maps; historical heuristic counters and budgets unchanged
descriptorSurface.limits: Candidate field origins only. Conditional configuration, generic props, indirect/re-exported factories and unsupported expressions require further tracing. No route, writer, reader, persistence, runtime visibility or functional parity is certified. Do not add these candidates to the historical totals: overlap is intentional and un-reconciled.

P0.title: Verification infrastructure
P0.intent: Make depth measurable and non-fakeable before changing any feature code.

P1.title: Suppression bugs and keyboard completion
P1.intent: Stop the client from overriding working server logic; finish the keyboard contract.
P1.note: Target corrected TWICE during implementation, both times because the metric was cruder than the intent. (1) 'all 66 txn pages' was wrong: 7 are header-only vouchers with no rows. (2) 'all 59 pages with a <tbody> map' was still wrong: 9 of those are read-only or fetched-data tables (bank reconciliation, rate matrix, scanned-tag list, reminders) where arrow/append/remove has nothing to act on. The measure is now pages holding a row ARRAY plus a blank-row factory - i.e. grids the operator authors - of which there are 50. Also corrected: the prior adoption count was 14, not 15; `purchase` had been counted because ExtendedGrid's doc comment contains the hook name.

P2.title: Shared sub-detail (stone/component) grid
P2.intent: One SubDetailGrid, adopted by every module that already persists *_IDTL rows.
P2.note: Column target corrected from 1000 to 790. The original assumed each of the 12 pages would carry its own duplicated per-cell markup, which is how the desktop grids are written. The implementation is a single shared SubDetailGrid declaring 35 columns from a registry, so on the UNION basis (distinct field surface built, the ratchet's basis) it contributes ~38 columns once, not 1000. Bulk column growth belongs to P7, where the main line grids gain genuinely distinct columns. Two metric changes were made here and are NOT progress: (a) declared column specs (`{ label: '...' }`) now count as columns, because a registry-driven header row renders real columns that a literal `<th>` count missed entirely; (b) a per-page basis is now reported beside the union — operatorSurfacePerPagePct, 2275/5107 = 44.5% at P2 start — because desktop's 5,107 is itself a per-form sum, making per-page the like-for-like read. The union remains the headline and the floor. The unreachable-field target moved from <=150 to <=177: P2's share of that reduction was the sub-detail fields themselves, and they are now all reachable (StoneSubDetailInput and TourStoneInput dropped off the worst-offenders list entirely, 192 -> 177). The remaining 177 are MfgLine 27, EnrollSchemeInput 18, RateCut 14 and the internal/server-derived interfaces, which are P3's scope; leaving them under P2 would have made P2 fail for work it was never doing. DEFERRED FROM P2-3: sales and sale-return still have no `stones` array. SL_IDTL already exists but the web writes ONE tag-identity row per line at ISR_NO 1, which other code consumes, while the desktop keys stone rows by SR_NO+ISR_NO within a line (TR_SALE.cs:14670, :21146 order by SR_NO, ISR_NO). Reconciling those two uses of the same table is a write-path change to a reversal-participating table and was not attempted without first pinning the desktop's ISR_NO semantics for the identity row.

P3.title: Wire every field the API already accepts
P3.intent: Eliminate capability that exists server-side and cannot be reached from a screen.
P3.note: Target corrected from <=40 to <=69, derived from web/parity/unreachable-triage.json rather than estimated. Of the 177 fields no screen can supply, only 108 are operator fields; 57 are server-derived and 12 are internal plumbing. The 57 are mostly posting-account slots (`*Ac`): WP-02D made account resolution fail closed against configured BOOK_DETL precisely so a request cannot name its own ledger, so exposing them as operator inputs would be a regression, not progress. Chasing <=40 would have required exactly that. 69 is therefore the FLOOR, reached when all 108 operator fields are wired. FLOOR MOVED 69 -> 73 during implementation, which makes the target EASIER and is therefore flagged: four more fields were reclassified out of `operator` with a stated reason each — ReverseInput.deleteLog (the reversal audit row is built by the posting engine), RepairApplyInput.loginCoCode (session company; a request asserting it could act on another company), WindowTileInput.mainName (window chrome, not voucher data) and RateCutInput.hdVchNo (hidden voucher number allocated by nextHiddenVoucherNoTx). Each reason is in triage_unreachable.py so the reclassification is reviewable rather than a silent loosening. FIELD WIRING COMPLETE: operator backlog 108 -> 8. Wired across this phase: MfgLine 27, EnrollSchemeInput 18, RateCut header+line 14, TourIssueLine 6, BatchReceiptLineInput 4, balance-sheet valuation 5, ItemOpeningLine 3, plus singletons on contra, fine-jv, ac-opbl, tag-cancel, tag-opening, tag-weight-diff, wholesale-sale-return, bullion, melting, KarigarForm and scheme. FLOOR MOVED 73 -> 82 by further reclassification, each with a reason in triage_unreachable.py and each flagged because it makes the target easier: the four *RojmelLine interfaces are day-book PROJECTION shapes the posting modules build themselves (karigar.ts:1212), not request contracts; and SettlementInput is the pure money/metal calculator's input, called with values rateCut.ts:957 has already derived. THE REMAINING 8 ARE NOT FIELD WIRING and are recorded as separate work: DesignBookLine 3 (pageNo/dieNo/ghatWt) needs P10's master child-grid; ChequeInput 2 (payee/acPayee) needs a cheque-print ACTION - GET /finance/cheque-print exists at routes/txn.ts:1299 and no page links to it; RateCutLine.isuRef needs a booking picker over available BUL_DATA rows; SchemeInstallment*.withUpi needs the desktop's UPI_DATA split-payment write (TR_MEMB_ENT.cs:2367-2397, :4620-4655) which the web does not have at all.

P4.title: Honour the settings the UI already offers
P4.intent: No setting may be editable and inert.
P4.note: PARTIAL. Root cause of ALL 74 inert settings was ONE omission: resolveSettingsBehaviorTx read CO_SET only, and every inert setting lives in CO_SET_NEW. Fixed with a second query; 21 fields added to the SettingsBehavior contract. A MISSING CO_SET_NEW row is deliberately not an error, because companies provisioned before that table existed have none and failing closed would take them down. DEFAULTS ARE PER-SETTING AND WERE EXTRACTED, NOT CHOSEN: MS_OPNCOMP.cs's blank-fill block gives NEGATIVE_STK_SALE -> 'Y' and LBR_WITH_GHT -> 'Y' (both PERMISSIVE) and TOT_FINE_STK_TYPE -> 'I'. A uniform blank-is-false default failed 20 existing sale tests, which were right. HONESTY NOTE ON THE 76: settings_parity.py counts a setting as honoured when business logic names it, and settingsBehavior.ts qualifies, so all 21 new fields count. Only FIVE have a flip-test proving an outcome changes: NEGATIVE_STK_SALE, SALES_WITH_HMTAX, PURC_WITH_HMTAX, PR_TDS_TAX, LBR_WITH_GHT. The other 16 are LOADED AND NOT YET CONSUMED. Honest reading is 60 effective + 16 waiting, not 76 effective. Each remaining one needs its consumer wired plus a flip-test before it may be called honoured. MONEY DEFECT FOUND VIA LBR_WITH_GHT: labourCharge('per_gram') was `netWt x rate` with no ghat term at all, while the desktop uses `(NetWt + GhtWt) x rate` by default (TR_SALE.cs:11112-11123). Every per-gram labour charge on a line carrying ghat weight was UNDERSTATED by ghat x rate. No test caught it because none combined ghat weight with a per-gram rate. Fixed in packages/core/src/calc.ts (ghatWt + withGhat on LabourInput) and threaded from sales.ts and purchase.ts computeLine via behavior.labourIncludesGhat. CONTINUATION: a documented semantic was WRONG and is corrected. `CUR_DAY_POSTING` is NOT a posting-date restriction, which is what its name suggests and what my first comment claimed. It is the STOCK-REBUILD scope: bound to a combo labelled Stock Refresh (UT_SETTING_MAIN.cs:9456 cboStkRefresh) and read in exactly two places, both about rebuilding MAIN_STOCK — MS_UPDATE.cs:2852-2868 rebuilds only from a chosen date forward when 'Y' and wipes every row when 'N', and Ac_Stock.cs:13 skips the opening-stock inserts when 'Y'. Renamed the contract field currentDayPostingOnly -> stockRefreshFromDateOnly and left it UNWIRED, because the web has no equivalent full stock-rebuild utility. Wiring it as a posting guard would have invented behaviour the desktop does not have. ALSO VERIFIED, not guessed: ITM_FINE_LOCK and SL_NWT_LOCK are pure UI read-only locks (TR_PURC.cs:7145-7148 sets TEXT_PR.ReadOnly = true). Nothing for the server to enforce — the value still posts, the operator may not retype it — so they are honoured on the SCREEN. New apps/web/lib/companySettings.ts provides useCompanySettings()/companyFlag() over the existing GET /settings (module-scope cache so a lock cannot flicker mid-entry; per-setting blankDefault because two desktop defaults are permissive). SL_NWT_LOCK applied to the sales net-weight cell; ITM_FINE_LOCK applied to purchase's fineWt via a new readOnlyFields prop on ExtendedBodyCells, which any extended column can now use. Desktop consumer counts confirmed for the remaining unconsumed settings: MsEstmateBankLock 23, MsSlNwtLock 11, MsSilverWt3Digit 10, MsItmWitLotStk 9, MsPurcLot 7, MsOldPurcTchGen 5, MsItmFineLock 2, MsOthItmWtRemove 2, MsTaxWithEstmate 2, MsSlAndTagWtDiff 1, MsTotFineStkType 1 — so none is speculative. TWO MORE SEMANTICS CORRECTED after verifying against the desktop rather than the column name — both had been documented from the name and both were wrong: (1) SL_TAG_WT_DIFF is NOT a permission ('permit a sale when the tag weight differs'). Ac_Stock.cs:125-130 shows that when 'Y' the desktop writes TWO extra MAIN_STOCK reconciliation rows per sale — ISR_NO 7 / VCH_SRNO 111 sign '-' carrying TAG_GWT-ITM_GWT when the difference is negative, and ISR_NO 8 / VCH_SRNO 222 sign '+' carrying ITM_GWT-TAG_GWT when positive, both gated on TAG_GWT <> 0. The 111/222 serials are sentinels for a reconciliation row, not real tag instances. Renamed saleTagWeightDiffAllowed -> saleTagWeightDiffReconciled and left unwired: it is a stock-writer change, and the semantics are now recorded so it cannot be built from the name. (2) ESTMATE_TAX verified at TR_SALE.cs:14168 — the tax master loads when the book type is 'T' OR the flag is 'Y', so a tax book always taxes and an estimate book taxes only when switched on. RUNNING TALLY OF NAME-DERIVED ERRORS I MADE AND CAUGHT: 3 of the 21 new contract fields had wrong documented semantics (CUR_DAY_POSTING, SL_TAG_WT_DIFF, and the earlier monthly-rate claim on dhiran). The lesson is that a CO_SET_NEW column name predicts its behaviour poorly, and every remaining unconsumed flag must be read in the desktop before it is wired.

P5.title: Per-cell recalculation kernel
P5.intent: One shared leave-cell dependency chain replacing per-page ad-hoc previews.
P5.note: STARTED. apps/web/lib/lineRecalc.ts created: the per-cell recalculation kernel, policy-driven ('sale' vs 'karigar', which genuinely differ — karigar folds ghat INTO the fine base then subtracts lessWt, TR_KR_ISU.cs:3933-3977 vs TR_SALE.cs:10693-10760). It DELEGATES to @datacare/core (metalAmount, labourCharge, fineWeight, round) instead of reimplementing, so client and server agree by construction; a second copy of the arithmetic is exactly how an on-screen total starts differing from the total that posts. 6 tests in apps/web/test/lineRecalc.test.ts, PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL: collapsing the karigar policy to the sale policy produced fine 8.7 instead of 9.62 and the test caught it. PREVIEW-DRIFT DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED ON THE SALES PAGE. Its local `calc` had been showing operators figures that were not the ones posting, in FOUR ways: fine rounded to 2dp where the server uses 3 (PRECISION.fine); westPct ignored entirely while the server's fine base is (touch + wastage); making computed as netWt x rate with NO ghat term — the same LBR_WITH_GHT understatement already fixed server-side, still live on screen; and local r2 rounding instead of the money kernel. Now delegates to recalcLine, so there is one implementation. WHY P5 MUST PRECEDE P7, measured not assumed: ~964 of the 3,508 desktop grid columns (27%) match a computed/roll-up naming pattern, so P7's 2,400 target is UNREACHABLE by wiring inputs — those columns have to be computed and displayed, which is this kernel's job. Confirmed concretely on TR_SALE: of its 57 named columns, 18 are absent from the web contract, and the karigar block among them (KR_LBR_RATE, KR_LBR_AMT, KR_GHT_WT, KR_OTH_AMT, KR_COST, KR_CON_WT) is NOT PERSISTED BY THE DESKTOP EITHER — Ac_Stock.cs posts literal 0,0,0 into MAIN_STOCK.KR_LBR_AMT/KR_OTH_AMT/KR_COST and only the 5 real SL_DETL karigar columns carry through, which the web writer already emits in full. Adding DB columns for them would have been wrong. ALSO CORRECTED: 6 TR_SALE columns I first reported as missing are present under different web names (ItmLot->itemLot, Design->designNo, Size->itmSize, LDisc%->discountPct, LDiscAmt->discountAmount, KrCode->karigarName). Guessing web names from desktop headers produced false gaps; the real SaleLineInput must be read. PRECISION SWEEP — the sales defect was NOT isolated. Thirteen pages derived fine weight with their own arithmetic. EIGHT rounded it to 2dp while PRECISION.fine is 3 (dhrn-issue, hallmark-sale, purchase-return, sale-return, purchase, estimate, purchase-hm, sales-order), so each displayed a fine weight that differed from the one that posted. Five more used a local r3 = Math.round((x+1e-9)*1000)/1000, a second rounding implementation (mfg-issue, mfg-receive, tour, fine-inout, tag-opening). All thirteen now call core's fineWeight. TWO wastage omissions found and fixed while doing it: purchase and tag-opening both carry westPct on their Line yet computed fine from touch alone, understating it — the server's fine base is (touch + wastage). NEW STRUCTURAL GUARD apps/web/test/derivedValueSources.test.ts. It scans every txn page and fails if one rounds fine to 2dp or derives fine inline without going through fineWeight/recalcLine. This earned its keep immediately: it caught purchase-hm and sales-order, which my own hand-written grep had MISSED because they name the row variable `r` rather than `l`. A one-time fix would have left both shipping wrong figures. Fail-proof performed: reintroducing the 2dp shape on estimate made the guard name 'estimate'. LABOUR PREVIEW DRIFT CAUSED BY MY OWN SERVER FIX. Eight pages compute per-gram labour locally as netWt x making and all send labourType 'per_gram', which the server now evaluates as (net + ghat) x rate after the LBR_WITH_GHT fix. Fixing the server therefore left previews behind. SCOPED PROPERLY RATHER THAN SWEPT: only TWO of the eight actually carry and send ghtWt (purchase, sales-order), so only those two understated labour by ghat x rate; the other six have no ghat field at all, making netWt x making correct there, and 'fixing' them would have been churn. Both now call core's labourCharge. The guard gained a fourth assertion covering this class, deliberately scoped to pages carrying ghat so it cannot produce that false positive. Fail-proof performed: reverting purchase to netWt-only labour made the guard name 'purchase'. PATTERN WORTH CARRYING FORWARD: a server-side correctness fix in this codebase can silently create a client-side disagreement, because the preview is a second implementation. That is the argument for recalcLine delegating to @datacare/core rather than restating the formulas.

P6.title: Discharge tag/stock containment
P6.intent: Five implemented workflows currently return 503; prove them or delete them.
P6.note: STARTED on tag-opening-update, the most tractable of the seven contained operations. LIVE DEFECT FIXED — the page half of P0-06. tag-opening/page.tsx sent `hallmarkId2: Number(line.hallmarkId2 || 0) || undefined` for all three secondary HUIDs. A HUID is ALPHANUMERIC: the contract types these as string (stockVoucherLifecycle.ts:61-63) and the writer stores text(...).slice(0, 10) (:647). So Number('AZ4567F') was NaN, `|| undefined` dropped it, and the id was SILENTLY LOST on every save. The reader had already been corrected and even documents the page doing this. The *_WT companions ARE numeric and were deliberately left alone. New guard apps/web/test/textIdentifiers.test.ts forbids Number() on nine string-typed identifiers across every txn page; fail-proofed by restoring the coercion, which made it name 'tag-opening'. SYMMETRY STRENGTHENED. tagOpeningRoundTrip.db.test.ts asserted the entire BAR_DETL row (>60 columns) but NOT BAR_IDTL, which editTagOpening deletes and rebuilds (:1264) and getTagOpening does not return — the exact shape of the write-without-read defect fixed five times here. I ALMOST RECORDED IT AS A SIXTH AND IT IS NOT ONE: those rows derive entirely from the same input.lines (one row per line at ISR_NO 1, :682-696), so an unchanged save reconstructs them. That was an ASSUMPTION; it is now an assertion, fail-proofed by blanking the reader's pcs, which made it name IT_PCS. CONTAINMENT DELIBERATELY NOT LIFTED. The testable engineering conditions of the gate now hold — symmetric create/get/update proven across BAR_DETL, BAR_IDTL, tag identity and stock movement, with designImageId ('IMG-0001-A') inside the asserted fixture so image association is covered. But the rule itself states that re-enabling 'requires a reviewed code change that cites the desktop-differential and safety evidence', and two things are outside what I can certify: an actual desktop-versus-web database diff needs the desktop application and its database, and lifting a fail-closed guard that exists to prevent silent data erasure on a live financial system is an OWNER decision, not a local edit. Evidence is recorded here; the rule stays until the owner reviews it. Deleting it myself would be the one move the containment design explicitly forbids. DISCHARGED with owner authorisation: tag-opening-update is removed from the registry, contained ops 7 -> 6. The rule required 'a reviewed code change that cites the desktop-differential and safety evidence satisfying its exit gate', and that is what this is — not a flag flip. Removed from parityContainmentOperations, the rule block, the route guard at txn.ts:3187, the page's block/notice/fieldset, and the three tests that asserted it. The discharge evidence is recorded IN containment.mjs so the history survives the rule. LIVE PROOF through Docker, which is what makes this more than green tests: PUT /stock/tag-opening/00001 previously returned 503 by design; it now reaches business logic. Created a tag with an alphanumeric HUID, reopened it (66 fields per line returned), fed the payload straight back as an operator pressing save would, and the row is unchanged — TAG_NO GOL000001, HM_ID2 'HUID9AB', DESIGN_NO 'D-TO-1', ITM_STYLE 'ST9', ITM_FINE 4.580 = 5 x 91.6%. That HUID is exactly what the old Number() coercion destroyed. The obsolete web test was INVERTED rather than deleted: it now fails if anything re-introduces a containment block, a disabled save, or a Number() coercion on the HUID — so the guarantee survives the rule it used to enforce. The skipped harness placeholder now points at tagOpeningRoundTrip.db.test.ts, which is stronger than what it would have asserted: full-row equality rather than a field list that could drift. The other SIX rules stay blocked and untouched; releasing one did not weaken them, and the registry still has intentionally no environment override. TAG-CANCEL, first gate clause satisfied: 'exact live identity'. The rule said the path 'can resolve historical availability instead of one live serial identity', and the code showed exactly how — two count queries keyed on CO_CODE + TAG_NO only. Three real consequences: (1) NO LC_CODE, so one branch could cancel another branch's stock; (2) no VCH_SRNO, so a tag number with several instances was judged on any historical row rather than the live one; (3) the test was `ITM_SIGN='-' EXISTS` rather than a net balance, so a tag sold and later RETURNED — the return posts '+' — was permanently un-cancellable although it sits in stock. Fixed by reusing issueTagTx, the same resolver a sale uses: it nets MAIN_STOCK signs per instance, excludes employee-issued tags, holds an advisory lock, and raises TagNotAvailable / TagIdentityAmbiguous instead of guessing. A cancel can therefore no longer disagree with a sale about what 'in stock' means. The out-movement now carries the RESOLVED VCH_SRNO, without which it nets against nothing. Two smaller corrections in the same path: fine was computed locally as netWt x touch / 100 and now goes through fineFor('tagOpening'), and ITM_WEST was hard-coded to 0 so a cancel disagreed with the tag it reverses — wastage now travels. TagCancelLine gained vchSrno (to disambiguate an instance), ghtWt and westPct. tagCancel had ZERO test coverage. New apps/api/test/tagCancelIdentity.db.test.ts covers all four behaviours and is fail-proofed: restoring the original guard fails 3 of the 4, including the cross-location case. Fixture traps hit and recorded: Postgres date columns need a Date object, not a string (42804), and VCH_TYPE is varchar(6) so 'SALERTN' overflows (22001). STILL BLOCKED. The gate also requires full cancel detail (BAR_CAN_DETL writes 17 of 76 columns), lifecycle/locks/reversal and a desktop database diff, so the rule stays until those are done too. TAG-CANCEL, second gate clause satisfied: 'full cancel detail'. BAR_CAN_DETL writes 17 -> 51 of its 76 columns, covering the desktop TR_TAG_CAN MSG grid (45 named columns): tag lot, design, counter, size, style, colour, polish, description, remark, HUID, the labour block, rate/amount/MRP/tag-cost, rate and PR codes, the karigar block, the design image and the target counter. The register is the audit trail for a cancelled tag, so holding a third of it meant the evidence of WHAT was cancelled was thinner than the tag itself. The resolved VCH_SRNO is now stamped on the register row as well as the stock movement — without it the register cannot say which instance of a repeated tag number was cancelled. Test extended to 5 cases and fail-proofed by nulling KR_NAME. The 25 columns still unwritten are header-derived or unused by this form (AC_CODE, ADD_USER, DATA_TRFR, the HM_ID2-4 set, ITM_COLOUR duplicate, ITM_CF_NO, TBL_POSTING), not operator fields. STILL BLOCKED, and two clauses remain: lifecycle/locks/reversal, and a desktop database diff. The diff needs the desktop application and its database, which I cannot run here — that is the one clause I expect to have to hand back rather than satisfy. TAG-CANCEL, third gate clause: lifecycle/reversal. deleteTagCancel reversed MAIN_STOCK and the register but did NOT restore the TAG_STOCK row that issueTagTx consumes. A BAR_DETL-backed tag recovers anyway because availability is a NET SUM and deleting the '-' makes it positive again — but a TAG_STOCK-only tag ended up in neither table, invisible to every availability query and therefore PERMANENTLY LOST. Fixed by mirroring the sale reversal: read the register BEFORE reverseVoucherTx deletes it, and restore only tags BAR_DETL cannot vouch for (restoring a BAR_DETL-backed tag too would make one physical tag issuable twice). Two tests, both directions asserted. A LATENT DEFECT IN THE SALE AND PURCHASE-RETURN PATHS, found while writing the fix. Both pushed IT_CODE into their legacy-restore payload, and TAG_STOCK has no IT_CODE column — it carries IT_TYPE. insertTagTx THROWS on an undeclared column by design ('anything outside it is a caller mistake'), so deleting a sale or a purchase return that consumed a TAG_STOCK-only tag aborted the ENTIRE reversal with `unknown TAG_STOCK column(s) IT_CODE`. Imported/legacy stock is exactly what that path exists for, so it was reachable and untested. Fixed in both. GUARD BUILT, THEN REBUILT TWICE — worth recording because the failures were instructive. Version one split on object literals and reported 57 offenders, nearly all unrelated DELETE_DATA and MAIN_STOCK rows; a guard that cries wolf gets ignored, so it was scoped to objects setting STK_TYPE: 'R' at restoreTagTx sites. Version two then flagged the very COMMENT documenting the fix, because `// NO IT_CODE: TAG_STOCK has IT_TYPE` matches `NAME:` as readily as code does — a scanner reading prose as code reports the explanation as the defect. It now strips comments first, and is fail-proofed by re-adding IT_CODE. TAG-WEIGHT-DIFFERENCE started. The path never looked the tag up AT ALL: it wrote a MAIN_STOCK movement keyed on TAG_NO alone, with no BAR_DETL, TAG_STOCK, resolver or VCH_SRNO anywhere in the function. So it would adjust the weight of a phantom tag, a tag belonging to another location, or one already sold, and the movement netted against no particular instance of a repeated tag number. Now resolves through resolveLiveTagIdentityTx and stamps the resolved VCH_SRNO. A DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS: this calls the RESOLVER, not issueTagTx. A weight change does not consume the tag, and issueTagTx deletes the TAG_STOCK row — reusing the cancel path here would have removed the tag from stock as a side effect of changing its weight. Same two smaller corrections as cancel: fine via fineFor('tagOpening') instead of a local netWt x touch / 100, and ITM_WEST no longer hard-coded to 0. TagWeightDiffLine gained vchSrno and westPct. Three tests, fail-proofed by stubbing the resolver — all three fail without it. MY FIRST ASSUMPTION WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE: I expected the desktop to UPDATE the tag's weight on BAR_DETL, and it does not. TR_TAG_WT_DIFF issues 5 UPDATE BAR_DETL and 5 UPDATE LBR_ISU_DETL statements, and they BACK-FILL THE KARIGAR COST BLOCK (KR_COST, KR_LBR_RATE, KR_LBR_AMT, KR_OTH_AMT) plus ITM_REMARK — each guarded by `if (Conversion.Val(mSG[i, N]) == 0.0)`, i.e. only when the operator left that cell blank, copying the value from the tag's existing record so the cost basis survives the weight change (TR_TAG_WT_DIFF.cs:10385-10392). It also writes TAG_PRINT_DATA twice (queue a tag reprint) and RATE_CUT_ISU_REC twice. Those branches are NOT implemented yet and are recorded here with their exact condition rather than guessed at, because five conditional back-fills invented from the column names is how the wrong-semantics mistakes earlier in this project happened. STILL BLOCKED: the gate needs the complete branch matrix, configured accounts, and the desktop database diff. INFERENCE RETRACTED, and recorded so nobody builds on it. Mid-investigation I concluded the desktop weight-difference voucher REPLACES the tag (writes a new BAR_DETL row under its own voucher key), reasoning from the delete block at TR_TAG_WT_DIFF.cs:8552 which removes BAR_DETL by VCH_NO. That is WRONG: the form contains ZERO `INSERT INTO BAR_DETL` — its only inserts are TAG_PRINT_DATA x2 and RATE_CUT_ISU_REC x2. The delete block also removes LBR_DATA, LBR_ISU_DETL, LBR_REC_DETL and BAR_IDTL, so it reads as a shared defensive cleanup block reused across forms rather than evidence of what this form writes. WHAT IS ACTUALLY VERIFIED. At :10360 the form reads the tag's existing KR_LBR_RATE, KR_LBR_AMT, KR_OTH_AMT, KR_COST and ITM_REMARK from BAR_DETL keyed on CO_CODE + LC_CODE + TAG_NO + VCH_SRNO. Then, per column, when the operator left that grid cell blank — mSG[i,43] KR_LBR_RATE, [i,44] KR_LBR_AMT, [i,45] KR_OTH_AMT, [i,46] KR_COST — it writes the existing value back with the SAME key. Against BAR_DETL that is a no-op; the paired `UPDATE LBR_ISU_DETL SET <col>` is NOT, so the real behaviour is SYNCING THE LABOUR-ISSUE DETAIL WITH THE TAG'S KARIGAR COST when the operator supplies nothing. NOT IMPLEMENTED, and deliberately so: the web's tagWeightDiff writes no LBR_ISU_DETL row at all, so the sync has no target. Implementing the back-fill alone would be dead code, and implementing the labour leg is a larger piece than this turn can verify properly. Stopping at a verified boundary rather than guessing is the same discipline that caught CUR_DAY_POSTING and SL_TAG_WT_DIFF meaning something other than their names. TAG-SPLIT INVESTIGATED, NOT IMPLEMENTED, and the containment rule's premise needs re-examining. The rule says the current split 'does not allocate child serials or create barcode detail, sub-detail, image, and parent-child lineage'. I set out to add child BAR_DETL rows and found the DESKTOP DOES NOT CREATE THEM EITHER. What TR_TAG_SPLIT actually does, each checked rather than inferred: its only INSERTs are TAG_SET x2, TAG_PRINT_DATA x2, RATE_CUT_ISU_REC x2 and USER_DATA x1 — no INSERT INTO BAR_DETL anywhere. Its shared stock routine Ac_Stock.Tag_Split_Stk (Ac_Stock.cs:403) writes MAIN_STOCK ONLY, which is exactly what the web writes. Its BAR_DETL usage is SELECTs to allocate the next TAG_SRNO (MAX(TAG_SRNO), CAST(TAG_SRNO AS INT), SUBSTRING(TAG_NO,4,5)) plus 2 DELETEs that belong to the voucher-delete path. AND THE TAG_SET INSERTS ARE NOT UNCONDITIONAL CHILD REGISTRATION: both sit inside a GRID EVENT HANDLER (mSG_PR.Col == 48, MsgPrClear, mSG_PR.Rows += 1), so they fire as the operator types rather than on save, and each is gated on a company setting — `if (MsTagRpt == "Y")` and `if (Module_Save.MsRendomTag == "Y")`. Both default to 'N' in MS_OPNCOMP.cs, so on a default company TAG_SET is never written at all. TAG_SET is a tag-print/random-tag queue, not the child identity registry the rule implies. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PHASE: the 175-column TR_TAG_SPLIT gap cannot be closed by 'create the child barcode rows the desktop creates', because it does not create them here. Discharging tag-split needs the rule's own premise checked against the desktop first — an owner-level question about what the split is supposed to produce — and I am not implementing against a description the source does not support. This is the FOURTH assumption of mine about the tag forms that the source contradicted (tag replacement, the karigar width count, the audit columns, and now child barcode creation). The pattern is that these forms look like their siblings and behave differently, so nothing here should be built from resemblance.

P7.title: Grid column completion on existing screens
P7.intent: The dedicated screens reach only 20% of desktop grid columns; close that.
P7.note: STARTED. Grid columns 1180 -> 1259 (+79), surface 2204 -> 2283, so 33.6% -> 35.9% of desktop columns and 43.2% -> 44.7% of surface. Two pages wired through the proven ExtendedGrid pattern: hallmark-sale (49 live fields of SaleLineInput, which had 59 of 72 unwired) and purchase-return (30 fields, mirroring purchase's registry; createPurchaseReturn takes PurchaseLineInput[] so all are accepted). Blank cells are OMITTED on submit, never sent as 0, because an explicit zero is an override at the writer. TARGETING IS NOW MEASURED, NOT GUESSED: richness_join.py keys desktop columns as gridNamedCols and web as gridColumns, so my first ranking query read 0 for every desktop form. Corrected, the real gap on forms WITH web surface is 2254 columns, worst first: TR_TAG_SPLIT 175 (contained until P6), TR_WH_SALE 116, TR_SALE_RTN 111, TR_TAG_WT_DIFF 90 (contained), TR_SALE_LBR 88, TR_SALE_ORD 85, TR_SALE_HM 84. DEAD-CELL DEFECT AVOIDED, and this is the finding that matters. I first exposed 61 fields on hallmark-sale and then audited each against the writer. TWELVE were dead or inappropriate: five have NO COLUMN IN SL_DETL at all despite the interface carrying a column comment (ITM_MARGIN, TAG_LBR_PRC, TAG_LBR_RATE, TAG_LBR_AMT, TAG_OTH_AMT — verified against information_schema); four are declared but never read by the writer (otherWt, itType, tagType, dataTransfer); three are internal serials the server assigns (tagSrNo, oldSrNo, vchSrno). `margin` is server-derived deliberately — sales.ts:1866 notes a client-supplied cost would let the margin be manipulated. Each would have been a cell that silently DISCARDS what the operator types, and would have inflated this metric with dead surface. Removed, with the reasoning recorded in the page so they are not re-added from the contract. fineWt, metalAmount and labourFixed ARE exposed because the writer honours each as an override (sales.ts:240, :264, :278). COROLLARY, now proven twice: presence on an API interface does NOT mean a field is persisted. purchase.ts:979 hard-codes ITM_SIZE: '' citing TR_PURC.cs:13106 and notes the desktop writes blank on 77/77 sampled vouchers — so purchase legitimately never stores a size. Any future column wiring must check the WRITER, not the interface. The structural guard caught my own new work twice: adding ghtWt to hallmark-sale and to purchase-return made each page's netWt x making labour preview wrong, and derivedValueSources.test.ts failed immediately both times. Both now use core's labourCharge. CONTINUED: wholesale-sale (24 RateCutLine fields, 0 dead) and sale-return (48 SaleLineInput fields) wired. Columns 1180 -> 1331, so 33.6% -> 37.9% of desktop columns and 43.2% -> 46.1% of surface. New scripts/writer_verified_fields.py audits a page against its WRITER, not its interface. It reproduced my manual hallmark-sale finding exactly (8 dead + 4 read-but-not-operator-input on sale-return) and is documented as a FILTER not an oracle, because it over-reports two ways I had to catch by reading source: otherWt is read as g.otherWt (an OLD-GOLD row, sales.ts:1512) not a sale line, and vchSrno is read (sales.ts:913) but is the server-assigned BAR_DETL tag identity. MY OWN KERNEL WAS WRONG, found by a live voucher. A sale return posted ITM_FINE 5.065 where lineRecalc predicted 4.605. The server's fine policy is (net + ghat) x (touch + west) / 100 with a pct === 0 -> net + ght fallback; my hand-written 'sale' policy dropped BOTH the ghat term and the fallback. There are TWELVE distinct desktop policies in finePolicy.ts, each cited (karigarIssue subtracts lesWt, karigarReceipt is net-only, itemOpening ignores ghat, purchaseOldGold subtracts lesTouch and adds kunFine). FIXED STRUCTURALLY, not locally: finePolicy.ts MOVED into @datacare/core with the api path left as a re-export, so there is exactly one implementation both sides import. lineRecalc's policy type is now the server's own FineWorkflow union. All 13 pages that derived fine were re-routed from the generic fineWeight(net, touch) to fineFor(<workflow>, ...) — the earlier sweep had fixed PRECISION but left the ghat omission on every one of them. The structural guard now requires fineFor, not fineWeight. RATCHET INTEGRITY: moving finePolicy dropped the kernel rounding-bypass count 108 -> 107 and the spread 69 -> 68, and two tests failed. That drop was RELOCATION, NOT IMPROVEMENT — the scan rooted at apps/api/src only, so the file's local round3 left scope while still existing. Lowering the ceiling would have been gaming my own ratchet, so kernelConformance.test.ts now scans packages/core/src as well and the counts are back to 108/69. The measure asks how many places reimplement a primitive; moving code must not change the answer. ALSO CONFIRMED FAITHFUL, not a bug: the book policy expects MAIN_BOOK 'SALES RETURNE' with a trailing E. The desktop uses that exact string 188 times and bookPolicy.ts:28 documents preserving it deliberately. FOURTH TRANCHE: estimate 48, mfg-order-issue 51, purchase-hm 37, mfg-receive 27 columns wired. Columns 1180 -> 1494 and surface 2204 -> 2518 across the phase, so 33.6% -> 42.6% of desktop columns and 43.2% -> 49.3% of surface. vp-parcel needed nothing (34/34 already wired) and wholesale-sale-return has only 6 left. GENERALISED after doing it five times by hand: scripts/wire_extended_columns.py performs all five steps (row interface, blank(), registry + numeric set, imports/state, header+body+toggle). It detects the page's conventions rather than assuming them — pages use Line/lines or Row/rows, and the row variable and per-field setter vary (l/setLine, r/setRow, r/set). Assuming produced TS2304 'cannot find name l' on two pages, which is why detection is now in the script. A CODEMOD MISTAKE WORTH RECORDING: my first submit-wiring anchor was `itCode: [^\n]*` which matched the INTERFACE DECLARATION (`itCode: string;`) rather than the request payload, producing TS1131 syntax errors in four files at once. Reverted and re-anchored on the payload map itself (`.map((x) => ({` and the destructured `.map(({ x, sourceIndex }) => ({` variant two pages use). Broad regex anchors over page source need a shape unique to the target, not a field name that appears in both the type and the payload. LIVE CONFIRMATION of the new columns through Docker: a purchase carrying convRate/convPct/commissionPct/lossWt/bagWt/itDesc/lotNo persisted as CONV_RATE 55, CONV_PRC 2, COMM_PRC 1.5, ITM_LOSS_WT 0.02, BAG_WT 0.05, IT_DESC 'HM ring', LOT_NO 'L9', with ITM_FINE 7.280 = 8 x 91%. lessTouch persists as ITM_LESS_TCH (purchase.ts:941, citing mSG_PR[i,23] :13121) — my first verification query guessed LESS_TOUCH and found nothing, which looked like a dead cell and was not. The structural guard fired again on estimate and purchase-hm the moment they gained ghtWt; both now use core's labourCharge. That is four separate pages it has caught mid-change.

P8.title: Missing workflows and screens
P8.intent: Lot manufacturing, rate-cut receive side, tour family, UAE variants.
P8.note: STARTED via a NEW DIAGNOSTIC that changed the plan: compare each detail table's WIDTH against the number of columns its writer populates. This found thin contracts over wide tables, and two tables with NO WRITER AT ALL. TR_SALE_LBR: contract 6 -> 41 fields; LBR_ISU_DETL has 113 columns and the writer populated ten while the desktop MSG grid has 30. Then LBR_REC_DETL (95 columns) turned out to have no writer at all — the desktop form has TWO item grids, mSG (labour billed) and mSG_PR (metal RECEIVED, referenced 268 times, 32 named columns). The web had no receive side whatsoever, so a labour bill settled with metal could not record what came in. Added LabourReceiptLine + receiveLines and the LBR_REC_DETL write. MIRROR-IMAGE DEFECT WORTH NAMING: LBR_REC_DETL was ALREADY in LABOUR_WRITE_TABLES, so the delete path had been cleaning up a table nothing ever populated — declared-but-never-written, the inverse of the written-but-never-read defect found five times earlier. TR_FN_INOUT: contract 6 -> 48 fields; the writer populated 16 of INOUT_DETL's 96 columns against a 42-column desktop grid. The module had ZERO test coverage, so apps/api/test/fineInoutGrid.db.test.ts is new (41 persisted-column assertions). Writing it exposed a real bug: PR_CODE is varchar(2) and EMP_ISU varchar(1), so realistic values aborted the whole voucher with a Postgres 22001. The writer now slices every narrow column to its true width, truncating as the desktop truncates instead of failing the save. THREE FIELDS DELIBERATELY NOT EXPOSED on the receive line: the desktop mSG_PR grid shows PsWt, HmFine and SlvFine but LBR_REC_DETL has no ITM_PCS_WT, HM_FINE or SLV_FINE column (checked against information_schema), so they would have been dead cells. FINE POLICIES ROUTED THROUGH THE SHARED TABLE, not reinvented: the labour issue line uses fineFor('sale'), and metal received uses fineFor('purchaseOldGold') — which subtracts less-touch from (touch + wastage) per TR_PURC.cs:7310-7317 — so a labour bill agrees with the purchase screen. Codemod hardened again: blank() exists both multi-line and as a SINGLE-LINE literal, and the multi-line regex silently missed the latter, which is the same gotcha that produced missing-comma syntax errors on three pages earlier. It now handles both. I CAUGHT MYSELF COMMITTING THE DEAD-CELL DEFECT. The precise width diagnostic (count columns in each table's actual row builder, not the whole file) showed PR_DETL written by purchaseReturn.ts using 25 of 113 columns while purchase.ts writes 80 of the same table. That prompted a self-check of the 30 columns I had wired onto purchase-return in an earlier round by MIRRORING purchase's registry: 29 of the 30 were DEAD — the writer ignored them, so every cell silently discarded what the operator typed. I had verified them against PurchaseLineInput (the contract) instead of the writer, which is exactly the mistake this project has been guarding against, and I made it before writer_verified_fields.py existed. Fixed by making them real rather than deleting them, because the desktop does persist this detail on a return: 45 contract-backed columns added to the purchaseReturn detail writer. Dead count 29 -> 0. The last three (fineWt, kunFine, metalAmount) are live as CALCULATOR OVERRIDES rather than direct columns — purchase.ts:228, :230, :258 — so they are correctly exposed. Seven candidates were dropped during the fix because they are not on PurchaseLineInput or have no source in the module (designImageId, itmSize, karigarName, mcxRate), which is the check that keeps the fix from creating new dead cells. SEPARATE FINDING RECORDED, NOT HALF-FIXED: purchaseReturn writes no MAIN_USER, HD_VCH_NO or VCH_TIME on either header or detail, and PurchaseReturnInput has no `mainUser` field at all — so a purchase return carries NO user attribution and no hidden-voucher link, unlike a purchase. HD_VCH_NO is what TEMP_BOOK_DATA and the day-book join on. Fixing it needs a contract change plus hidden-voucher allocation, so it is written into the module as a comment and recorded here rather than patched halfway. KARIGAR COST BASIS ON CREATED TAGS — a money-adjacent defect with the evidence already in the codebase. stock.ts:88-93 records a measurement from the real customer database: a SALE LINE COPIES KR_NET_WT / KR_TOUCH / KR_FINE FROM THE TAG, equal on 102 of 102 tagged sale lines, and NOT derivable (KR_NET_WT x KR_TOUCH/100 fits only 7 of 92 rows) — the tag is the only source. The sale path was already selecting those columns. But karigar.ts, the writer that CREATES tags from a karigar receipt, wrote NONE of them, so every karigar-made tag produced a sale line with a ZERO karigar cost basis, which is what profit reporting is built on. Now writes KR_NET_WT, KR_TOUCH, KR_WEST_PRC and KR_FINE (via fineFor('karigarReceipt') — net-only x (touch + wastage), MS_UPDATE.cs:2691), plus ITM_WEST_PRC, ITM_GHT_WT and ITM_MRP so the tag can reproduce its own fine. AN EXISTING INVARIANT CAUGHT ME OVERREACHING. I also added MAIN_USER and HD_VCH_NO opportunistically, and mfgLifecycle's 'keeps a tagged karigar receipt intact across reopen and save unchanged' failed: on an EDIT the ORIGINAL creator must be preserved, and writing input.mainUser overwrote 'mfg-user' with the editor's value. Reverted both columns with the reason recorded in the code. The write path already stamps attribution, so the explicit column was not an improvement but a regression — and the distinction between the two is exactly what that test exists to enforce. Kept only the evidence-backed KR block. Also corrected my own diagnostic: the width scan reported karigar writing 10 of 110 BAR_DETL columns; the real figure was 23 because the scan could not see through `karigarBarcodeRows(...)` being a function call rather than an inline map. It is now 30. PURCHASE RETURN NOW RECORDS WHO DID IT. This was the finding deferred earlier, now closed: the writer had ZERO assignments of MAIN_USER, HD_VCH_NO or VCH_TIME on header or detail — the only matches in the file were my own comment about it — while purchase.ts has 13 and PR_DATA carries all three columns. So a voucher that reverses stock AND money had no attribution and no hidden-voucher link, and HD_VCH_NO is what TEMP_BOOK_DATA and the day book join on, meaning return rows could not be joined back. Added `mainUser` to PurchaseReturnInput, allocated the hidden series with nextHiddenVoucherNoTx AFTER the book resolves (the series is per book), and stamped all three on header and detail. Test asserts the detail's HD_VCH_NO equals the header's, and is fail-proofed. A DIAGNOSTIC BUILT AND DISCARDED IN THE SAME TURN, recorded so it is not rebuilt. I tried to generalise the karigar find — 'columns a reader SELECTs that no writer sets' — and it reported 69 for SL_DETL and flagged KR_FINE/KR_NET_WT/KR_TOUCH as unwritten. Both were false: all six SL_DETL columns I spot-checked ARE written by sales.ts, and I had written the three KR columns an hour earlier. The scan could not associate a writer with its table when the row builder is a function call, and it read joined columns (IT_NAME from ITEM_MAST) and even table names as columns. Discarded rather than acted on, because a scan with false positives in this codebase leads to DELETING working columns — the same trap that nearly removed 41 live fields when the dead-cell audit first ran. ATTRIBUTION SWEEP, evidence-first this time. Having fixed purchase-return, I checked every voucher module for the same shape and VERIFIED THE COLUMNS EXIST BEFORE TOUCHING ANYTHING — the discipline the discarded reader/writer diagnostic taught. Confirmed: INOUT_DATA, INOUT_DETL, MLT_DATA and MLT_DETL all carry MAIN_USER, HD_VCH_NO and VCH_TIME, and fineInout.ts and melting.ts assigned ZERO of them. Both fixed. A Fine In/Out moves metal between the company and a refinery, so an unattributed one is a metal movement nobody owns; a melt destroys one item's weight and creates another's. The hidden series is allocated per book in each case, and the detail rows share the header's HD_VCH_NO so a line can be traced to its voucher — asserted explicitly, not assumed. THREE MODULES LEFT ALONE, deliberately: batchReceipt.ts, stock.ts and tagSplit.ts. stock.ts writes TAG_STOCK, whose declared column set (TAG_STOCK_COLUMNS) has no MAIN_USER slot for the row builder in question and which THROWS on an undeclared column — adding one would abort the write, which is exactly the IT_CODE defect found earlier today. tagSplit is under containment and its writer is due to be rebuilt for the child-serial work, so patching attribution now would be thrown away. batchReceipt needs its table checked first; it is recorded rather than guessed at.

P9.title: Report parity
P9.intent: 18 missing report workflows plus parameter richness on the generic engine.
P9.note: STARTED with the HUID hallmark register — the first of the missing desktop report workflows, chosen because RP_HUID gives an unambiguous specification and needs no inference, which the tag forms did not. Report slugs 48 -> 49. Columns are the desktop's verbatim, taken from RP_HUID.cs: CoCode, VchTyp, VchNo, VchDate, TagNo, ItCode, Counter, Qty (the LITERAL 1 — one row is one tag), Pcs, Grwt, NetWt, then the four HUID slots each paired with its weight (HM_ID/HM_ID_WT .. HM_ID4/HM_ID4_WT), KrName, Book, BookName, ItRemark and TagId (= VCH_SRNO). Four slots exist because one tag can carry up to four hallmarked components. Two tabs mirror the desktop's variants: 'all' from BAR_DETL alone, and 'stock' which uses the SAME net-sign availability rule as the sale path, so the register cannot disagree about what is sellable — a plain 'no minus movement exists' test would wrongly drop a tag that was sold and returned. I USED THE DESKTOP'S OWN MENU CAPTION rather than inventing one. My first attempt registered 'Reports/HUID (Hallmark Register)', and the RBAC form catalogue rejected it: `route policy references unknown form`. The catalogue is built from the desktop menu, and MDI_FORM.cs calls the caption 'HuId Report' — including its own capitalisation. Registered under that. Three existing tests enforced this (slug count, canonical form mapping, and the view/print matrix), which is why the invented name could not slip through. THE RATCHET CAUGHT MY OWN NEW FILE. I wrote a local `r3 = Math.round((n + 1e-9) * 1000) / 1000`, and kernelConformance reported rounding bypasses 108 -> 109. The ceiling may only shrink, so the fix was to use the money kernel's round(n, PRECISION.weight), not to raise the ceiling. VERIFIED ON REAL DATA through the live stack: GET /api/reports/huid/export.csv returns 24 columns with actual alphanumeric HUIDs from the customer database (TKU6VX, MT1CD6, XX12N1) paired with their weights, karigar names and tag serials. Those ids all contain letters, so they are exactly the values the Number() coercion fixed earlier in this session would have destroyed — the report and that fix validate each other. SECOND REPORT: item weight-band labour levels (RP_STK_LEVEL, desktop caption 'ItStk Level'). Slugs 49 -> 50. THE NAME MISLEADS AND I CHECKED BEFORE BUILDING — 'level' is NOT a reorder level. ITM_WT_MAST holds LABOUR RATES BANDED BY WEIGHT per item (FROM_WT, TO_WT, MIN_PCS, LBR_TYPE, LBR_RATE, LBR_PRC, LBR_AMT, MIN_LBR_PRC, GHT_PRC, optional IT_DESIGN), so the report answers 'which making charge applies to a piece of this weight' — what an operator quoting a price needs. Had I built from the name I would have produced a min/max stock report the desktop does not have. The desktop's driving query (SELECT A.*, B.IT_NAME, B.IT_TYPE FROM ITM_WT_MAST A LEFT JOIN ITEM_MAST B) is reproduced rather than reinvented. The web already MAINTAINED this master (masters/labourUpdate.ts) but had no way to read it back, so the rates being charged were only visible one row at a time in a master screen. REPORT SELECTION WAS DELIBERATE: I ranked the missing desktop reports by query count and took a tightly specified one (9 queries) rather than RP_TRADING (3,321 lines, 18 queries, a full financial statement), because a partial financial statement is worse than none. RP_TRADING is recorded as needing its own pass: its core is fine-weight in/out aggregated from MAIN_STOCK by ITM_SIGN and IT_TYPE, plus rate-cut fine from AC_DATA by SIGN. VERIFIED PROPERLY: the first live call returned HTTP 200 with ZERO rows because ITM_WT_MAST was empty for the company, and an empty result proves nothing — so I seeded three bands (0-10 at 45/g, 10-25 at 40/g, 25-100 at 35/g design-specific) and confirmed all three come back with the right item name, type, band boundaries, rate and ghat percentage, then removed them. Rounding goes through the money kernel from the start this time, after the HUID report tripped the bypass ratchet. THIRD REPORT: bill-wise profit (RP_BILL_PROFIT, caption 'Bill Wise Profit'). Slugs 50 -> 51. THIS IS THE CONSUMER THAT MADE THE KARIGAR FIX MATTER. The desktop query joins MAIN_STOCK to BAR_DETL and takes KR_NET_WT, KR_FINE, KR_LBR_AMT, KR_OTH_AMT and KR_COST FROM THE TAG — profit is realisation minus the tag's karigar cost basis. While karigar.ts wrote none of those columns, every karigar-made tag would have reported ZERO cost here, which reads as pure profit. The live output now shows real tagged sales on the 'karigar-fine' basis with karigarNetWt 8.71 / karigarFine 8.414 carried from the tag. THE PROFIT FORMULA IS NOT REIMPLEMENTED: sales/billProfit.ts already holds the desktop's four-branch rule and the report calls lineProfit directly, so it cannot disagree with what the sale screen shows. The 'none' branch is surfaced as `unknownCost` in the totals rather than folded in as zero — a row whose cost cannot be established is not a zero-cost row, and reporting it as full profit is how a bad margin looks like a good one. MY OWN FILTER WAS WRONG AND THE LIVE OUTPUT CAUGHT IT. I filtered on ITM_SIGN='-' alone; the desktop uses THREE conditions — ITM_SIGN='-' AND TR_TYPE='S' AND TAG_NO <> 'N'. The first run therefore included tag-generation movements (VCH_TYPE 'TGEN'), which are OUT movements with no realisation, so they appeared with large NEGATIVE profits (-686.95, -342.35) dragging the total down, plus untagged lines costed from average touch alone. Fixed to the desktop's clause. Reading the OUTPUT rather than the HTTP status is what found this — a 200 with plausible-looking CSV was hiding a wrong measure. ALL THREE REPORTS NOW HAVE TESTS: apps/api/test/p9Reports.db.test.ts, 5 cases (161 files / 1373 tests). I wrote them BEFORE adding a fourth report, because the bill-profit defect showed the risk plainly — that one shipped a wrong measure behind an HTTP 200 and plausible-looking CSV, and only reading the output caught it. Live verification finds defects; it does not prevent their return. BOTH KEY CASES ARE FAIL-PROOFED. Removing the TR_TYPE/TAG_NO conditions makes the filter test report 3 rows instead of 1, which is precisely the tag-generation and untagged rows that produced negative profits against real data. Coercing the HUID with Number() makes the text assertion fail with `expected NaN to be 'HUID7AB'` — the exact failure mode fixed on the tag-opening page earlier today, so the report test now guards the page fix as well. The profit test asserts the karigar basis comes from BAR_DETL (KR_NET_WT 10, KR_FINE 9) rather than the movement, which is the column set karigar.ts failed to write; without it the row would report zero cost and therefore pure profit.

P10.intent: Child grids, conditional validation, per-parent collections.

P11.title: Parity certification
P11.intent: Operator depth equals the desktop; nothing inert, unreachable or contained.

Nine columns on sales were read by NOTHING — five have no SL_DETL column at all (ITM_MARGIN, TAG_LBR_PRC, TAG_LBR_RATE, TAG_LBR_AMT, TAG_OTH_AMT), tagSrNo/tagType are server-assigned, margin is deliberately server-derived, and dataTransfer/lineDiscountAmount are unread. metricChanges.attribution: This LOWERS the reported number and breaches the previous floor. It is a MEASUREMENT CORRECTION, not a regression: no working column was removed. The old floor was wrong because it counted 9 dead cells as parity. Re-baselined deliberately. The audit found 50 candidates initially; following each writer's own relative imports one level removed 41 false positives, because a module often delegates line building to a sibling (purchaseReturn -> purchase.ts's computeLine, which honours fineWt/kunFine/metalAmount as OVERRIDES rather than columns; salesReturn -> sales.ts). Reading only the named module would have deleted 41 working columns. Now gated: pnpm depth:deadcells, wired into CI beside depth:parity, fail-proofed by adding a fake column and watching it fail.

They are replaced by TagNotAvailableError ('tag not available for issue: <tag>') and TagIdentityAmbiguousValidationError from stock.ts, which are raised by a resolver that nets stock per instance and holds an advisory lock.

Validation did not shrink: two weak local messages became two shared errors already counted in stock.ts, so the enforcement is stricter while the tally is lower. The metric counts message strings per module and cannot see that a removed guard was replaced by a better one elsewhere. endToEnd.stack: docker compose: postgres 16 + api (Fastify) + web (Next.js 15), images built from Dockerfile.api/.web
endToEnd.provenWorkflow: Real operator path exercised against the running stack, not a test harness: POST /api/auth/login through the WEB container's proxy (argon2 password, httpOnly cookies) -> POST /api/purchases -> GET /api/purchases/:vchNo -> row confirmed in PR_DATA/PR_DETL. Arithmetic verified against the desktop formulas: net 10.000, touch 91.6, ghat 1.000 -> fine 10.076, metal 60456, labour 550, total 61006.
endToEnd.confirmsLbrWithGht: The live voucher returned labourAmount 550 = (10 + 1) x 50, so the LBR_WITH_GHT ghat fix is proven in a running application and not only in unit tests. Before that fix this line would have charged 500 and understated the bill by 50.
endToEnd.orderOfDiscovery: Each failure the stack returned was the app failing CLOSED and was correct behaviour: weak JWT_SECRET refused at boot (runtime config guard); tenant header ignored because allowTenantHeader is !isProduction; scope-incomplete until YEAR_MAST existed; 'requires ... configured book' until BOOK_DATA/BOOK_DETL existed; 'exactly one CO_SET behavior row' when I created a duplicate. Only the last failure was a real defect.

defectFound.symptom: POST /purchases omitting taxRatePct returned HTTP 500 "[DecimalError] Invalid argument: undefined".
defectFound.why: PurchaseInput.taxRatePct is declared a required number, but routes/txn.ts copies body.taxRatePct through untouched, so undefined entered the money pipeline and surfaced as an unhandled 500 that named no field. An operator would see only 'Internal Server Error'.
defectFound.whyTheSuiteMissedIt: Every fixture supplies a complete header, so 1349 passing tests could not see it.
defectFound.fix: requirePurchaseNumber() in purchase.ts, applied at both createPurchase and editPurchase. It accepts numeric strings because HTML fields arrive as strings, and DELIBERATELY does not default to 0 — a silent 0 would post a tax-free bill for a company that charges tax and put a wrong figure on a GST return, which is worse than a refusal.
defectFound.verified: Live: HTTP 500 [DecimalError] -> HTTP 400 'purchase requires a numeric taxRatePct; received nothing'. Regression test added to purchase.lifecycle.db.test.ts and PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL — with the guard removed it reproduced the exact DecimalError.

endToEnd.localDevChanges: Recorded so they are not mistaken for app changes: the compose volume's postgres passwords were realigned to .env (the volume was initialised with older ones), .env's JWT_SECRET was rotated to a random 96-char value because the API correctly refuses known-weak secrets, and a test company/operator/year/book/account/item set was seeded under tenant 'default'. .env is gitignored.
